class: T4 per-kernel attribution (same-ELF, same-nsys, back-to-back; no ceiling claim)
method: nsys profile --trace=cuda on the orin-release ELF (commit 5f625d8); decode phase = the last 256 attention_scores calls (16 steps x 16 full-attention layers); per-kernel GPU-busy time summed inside that phase, /16 steps. Baseline = no env var (bit-exact unroll-128 values kernel); split = Q3X_ENABLE_SPLIT_VALUES=1.
nsys_note: nsys (CUPTI) inflates memory-bound kernels vs the non-profiled e2e runs (baseline non-profiled decode 2894.9 ms vs nsys 2940.2; split non-profiled 2478.1 vs nsys 2526.0). Absolute per-kernel values are therefore nsys-relative; only the same-environment delta is meaningful.
findings: The split path is confirmed active in the full model: attention_values_exact runs 0 times under the env var, attention_values_split_shared runs 255 times (16 layers x 16 steps, minus 1 boundary).

The entire -27.79 ms/step kernel-time delta is the values-kernel swap (exact 50.48 -> split 22.79, -50.48) plus the +0.07 finalize; every other kernel moves <0.05 ms/step (noise). No hidden cost, no cross-kernel interference.

The nsys delta (-27.79 ms/step) matches the non-profiled e2e delta (2894.9-2478.1 = 416.8 ms / 15 steps = 27.8 ms/step) to within 0.1 ms, so the per-kernel attribution is consistent with the wall-clock result.

In the full model (nsys) the unroll-128 values kernel is 50.48 ms/step (3.16 ms/layer) and the split kernel is 22.79 ms/step (1.42 ms/layer). The isolated microbenchmark (2.799 / 1.689 ms/layer) is a different, lower-contention measurement; do not mix the two.
The earlier T4 figure 'values 111.7 ms/step' was the unroll-8 era (HEAD 56012ee); unroll-128 already cut it to 50.48 ms/step in this same nsys environment.
no_ceiling_claim: This record reports measured per-kernel times and their delta only. It makes no hardware-ceiling or target-reachability claim; the premise numbers behind the earlier ceiling analysis (182.5 GB/s pure-read, 18.52 GB/step weight read, 101.5 ms floor) are themselves unverified measurements and are flagged for re-measurement rather than assumed.
evidence: .q3x-work/evidence/split-nsys-20260927/ (split-p40.nsys-rep, split-p40.sqlite, preflight.json, response.txt) and .q3x-work/evidence/baseline-nsys-20260927/ (baseline-p40.nsys-rep, baseline-p40.sqlite, response.txt)
scores_kernel_followup: UPDATE 2026-09-27: the 'scores kernel as next candidate' framing was a prediction, not a measurement. The isolated microbenchmark (qwen36-27b-decode-scores-split-microbench-2026-09-27.json) shows the scores kernel is NOT DRAM-bandwidth-bound (40.5 GB/s effective 1x K vs the 182.7 GB/s ceiling); a bit-exact split-chunk variant buys only 1.14x per layer and is rejected as a production direction.
